title: Former lawmaker, deputy prosecutor arrested for alleged DUI - NewsBreak
text:
By Cate Piper Labas ,
7 hours ago
HONOLULU (KHON2) — It’s not the first time this former lawmaker and deputy prosecutor has been arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence.
Former deputy prosecutor Karamatsu found guilty of second DUI According to HPD, the latest arrest of Jon Riki Karamatsu happened just after 10 p.m. on Monday, Feb. 16, in Kalihi near the H-1 onramp.
The 51-year-old lawyer and business owner was arrested in 2007 during his term in the State House after a crash on the Moanalua Freeway and again in 2015 in Waikiki.
“Unfortunately, what happens is that oftentimes people who have been convicted once for DUI offend more than once,” Legal Analyst Doug Chin said.
Because of the number of years in between incidents, this arrest does not qualify Karamatsu as a habitual offender, which is someone with three offenses within 10 years and can lead to felony charges.
“You would expect and hope that when somebody gets convicted for driving under the influence or operating while they’re impaired, they will learn their lesson, and they will either do their community service and go to the classes that they need to do, and that’s good enough,” Chin said.
Karamatsu resigns as deputy prosecutor after 2nd DUI arrest KHON2 reached out to Karamatsu and one of his former attorneys for comment, but has not heard back.
Meanwhile, State lawmakers advanced a measure that would lower the legal limit of blood alcohol content to be considered impaired.
